mainTopic: Restoring a כהן through witnesses who came separately, and whether a woman jailed by gentiles stays permitted to her husband.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a case. One witness said a man is a כהן, so the court raised him up. Two witnesses then said he is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, so the court brought him down. Then another single witness said he is a כהן. The first explanation says everyone agrees the two single witnesses join together, and the argument is only about זילותא דבי דינא, disrespect to the court when it reverses itself. רב אשי rejects this, since then they should argue even about two witnesses against two. Instead, he says they argue about whether witnesses who testify at different times can be joined, which matches a ברייתא where רבי יהושע בן קרחה requires testifying together and רבי נתן allows separate days. A new משנה then rules that a woman jailed by gentiles over money stays permitted to her husband, but one jailed over a capital matter is forbidden. רב limits the leniency to times of Jewish power, and רבא challenges him from a woman held as collateral in אשקלון, a gentile-ruled city. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the case: up, down, and another witness
steps.stepSummary: The case is described step by step. A man was raised to כהונה through one witness and brought down through two. Then a second single witness says he is a כהן. Everyone agrees the two single witnesses join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we raised him up. Then two came and said he is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, and we brought him down. Then one witness came and said, 'I know he is a כהן.' Everyone agrees that witnesses join together for testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the description of the case where the argument takes place. This sets up the next step, which explains what the תנאים actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two single witnesses who said he is a כהן, one before the demotion and one after. This explanation assumes everyone agrees these two can be counted together as a full pair. So the argument cannot be about joining witnesses; it must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: we raised him up (to the status of a כהן)
we brought him down (removed him from כהונה)
son of a divorced woman and a כהן; he is a חלל and not fit for כהונה
son of a woman who had חליצה and a כהן; also unfit for כהונה
they join together to make one testimony

phrases.english: and we raised him up.
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of the case: one witness had said he is a כהן, so the court raised him up.

phrases.english: Then two came and said:
He is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a חלוצה,
and we brought him down.
Then one witness came and said:
I know about him that he is a כהן.
And everyone agrees that they join together for testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the case description that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the disputed case, two single witnesses said he is a כהן, separated by a demotion through two witnesses. Everyone agrees single witnesses combine.

steps.title: The argument is about embarrassing the court
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא will not raise him again, because flip-flopping makes the court look foolish. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the court can bring him down and raise him up, and does not worry about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they argue about whether to worry about disrespect for the court. The תנא קמא holds: once we brought him down, we do not raise him again, because we worry about disrespect for the court. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds: we brought him down and we raise him up, and we do not worry about disrespect for the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the two sides argue about, according to this first approach. The issue is זילותא דבי דינא, whether the court looks bad when it keeps changing its ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that, by the rules of testimony, there are now two witnesses saying he is a כהן. The only question is whether reversing a court decision hurts the court's dignity enough to stop it. The תנא קמא says yes; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the truth matters more.

keyTerms.meaning: disrespect or embarrassment to the court
we are concerned / we worry about it
the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה or ברייתא
they argue about

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּמֵיחַשׁ לְזִילוּתָא דְבֵי דִינָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: And here they argue about worrying over disrespect to the court.
The first תנא holds:
Once we brought him down, we do not raise him up,
because we worry about disrespect to the court.
And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן אַחֲתִינַן לֵיהּ וַאֲנַן מַסְּקִינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: We brought him down, and we raise him up,
and we do not worry about disrespect to the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּמֵיחַשׁ לְזִילוּתָא דְבֵי דִינָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having said both sides agree witnesses combine, it now names the real point of argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא does not restore him, out of concern for the court's dignity. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל restores him and ignores that concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: זילותא דבי דינא is a real consideration that comes up in other places. Here the גמרא tests whether it can explain this argument.

steps.title: רב אשי: then they should argue even with full pairs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects. If the issue is only embarrassing the court, the same problem would exist when two witnesses demote him and then two others restore him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: If so, then even with two against two they should also argue!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the explanation from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Disrespect to the court comes from the court reversing itself. That happens no matter how the witnesses arrive. So why describe the case with single witnesses who came one at a time? The argument should apply even to two full pairs, so the single-witness case would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged it strongly
if so
two (witnesses) against two (witnesses)

phrases.english: רב אשי challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תְּרֵי וּתְרֵי נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, then even with two and two they should also argue!
phrases.notes: Two witnesses bring him down, then two others raise him up. The court still reverses itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation that the argument is about disrespect to the court.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנאים argue over זילותא דבי דינא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Disrespect to the court does not depend on whether the witnesses were single or paired. So the case of single witnesses would be pointless, and the argument should extend to two against two.

steps.title: רב אשי's new explanation: joining separate witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the real argument is whether two single witnesses who came separately can be joined into one testimony. This is the same argument found between תנאים elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: They argue about whether witnesses join together for testimony, and it is the same as the argument of these תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first explanation, רב אשי gives a completely different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first approach said everyone agrees the witnesses combine. רב אשי says the opposite: that is exactly the point of argument. The side that restores him holds that the two single witnesses count as a pair. The side that does not restore him holds that they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (dropping the earlier explanation)
an argument or dispute
תנאים, the sages of the משנה era

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two approaches. The first said everyone agrees the witnesses join together. רב אשי says joining them together is the very thing they argue about.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
They argue about whether witnesses join together for testimony,
and it is in the argument of these תנאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was knocked down in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the explanation of what the תנאים argue about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees single witnesses combine, and the argument is about disrespect to the court.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether separate single witnesses combine into one testimony. That is why the case involves single witnesses and not two against two.

steps.title: The ברייתא about witnesses who saw separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the argument between תנאים. The first view says witnesses combine only if they saw the event together. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says they combine even if they saw it one after the other, but they must testify in court together.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Their testimony does not join together unless both of them saw it together as one. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: even if one saw after the other. But their testimony is not established in court unless both of them testify together as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that רב אשי was pointing to, where the תנאים argue about joining witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view requires the two witnesses to see the event at the same time. רבי יהושע בן קרחה allows them to see it at different times. Even he still requires the two of them to testify in court together, so in our case, where the single witnesses testified at different times, he would not combine them.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
together, as one
one after the other
is established / is accepted (in court)

steps.whatToRemember: First approach: everyone agrees the witnesses join together, and the argument is about disrespect to the court. רב אשי rejected it, because then two against two should also be argued. His approach: the argument is whether separate witnesses join together, which matches an argument between תנאים in a ברייתא. The next step finishes that ברייתא with רבי נתן's view, which is the one that fits our case.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Their testimony does not join together
unless the two of them saw it together, as one.
רבי יהושע בן קרחה says:
Even if this one saw after that one.
But their testimony is not established in court
unless the two of them testify together, as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין עֵדוּתָן מִצְטָרֶפֶת עַד שֶׁיִּרְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב אשי's claim that this is an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the argument is about joining separate witnesses together.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the first view requires the witnesses to see together, while רבי יהושע בן קרחה allows seeing one after the other but requires testifying together.

steps.title: רבי נתן: the court may even hear the two witnesses on different days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the most lenient view. רבי נתן says the court can hear one witness today and the other tomorrow, and their testimony still joins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: The court hears this witness's words today, and when the second witness comes tomorrow, the court hears his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step finishes with a third, most lenient view. רבי נתן says the two witnesses do not even have to testify in court together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has three views: the witnesses must see the event together; they may see it separately but must testify together (רבי יהושע בן קרחה); or they may even testify on different days (רבי נתן). So the תנא קמא of our case, who does not restore him, holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who restores him, holds like רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: The court hears his words (accepts his testimony)
His fellow, meaning the second witness
Tomorrow, meaning at a later time

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on joining single witnesses: they must see it together; they may see it separately but must testify together (רבי יהושע בן קרחה); or they may see it and testify at separate times (רבי נתן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
We hear the words of this one today,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the first witness. Here "we" means the court.

phrases.english: and when his fellow comes tomorrow
we hear his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 5 with a third opinion.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the dispute about the כהן depends on an argument between תנאים over joining separate single witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with three views on joining witnesses, ending with רבי נתן.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman imprisoned by gentiles
steps.stepSummary: A woman jailed by gentiles over a money matter stays permitted to her husband. A woman jailed over a capital matter becomes forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who was imprisoned by gentiles: if it was because of money, she is permitted to her husband. If it was because of a capital crime, she is forbidden to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. It rules on whether a woman held in a gentile prison stays permitted to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on why she was jailed. If it was over money, the captors want to be paid, so we do not suspect she was violated. If it was over a capital crime, her life is in danger, so we suspect what happened there and she is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Was imprisoned
Because of a money matter
Because of a capital matter (a matter of life and death)
Permitted to her husband
Forbidden to her husband

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A woman who was imprisoned by gentiles,
because of money — she is permitted to her husband.
because of a capital matter — she is forbidden to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jailed over money: permitted to her husband. Jailed over a capital matter: forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: רב limits the משנה to a time of Jewish control
steps.stepSummary: רב says the money-case leniency applies only when Jews hold power. When the gentiles are in control, even a woman jailed over money is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: The משנה taught this only when the Jewish people's hand is strong over the nations. But when the nations' hand is strong, even if she was jailed over money, she is forbidden to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב, who narrows the משנה's leniency. He says it applies only in certain political conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's reason for leniency is that her captors hold back out of fear. רב says that fear exists only when Jews are in power. When gentiles rule, nothing holds the captors back, so even in a money case she is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only (in a certain case)
A strong hand, meaning power or control
The nations of the world

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the sugya. The next objections all test whether רב's limit fits other sources.

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said that Rav said:
They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל תַּקִּיפָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: when the hand of Israel is strong over the nations of the world,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יַד אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם תַּקִּיפָה עַל עַצְמָן,
phrases.english: but when the hand of the nations of the world is strong over themselves,
phrases.notes: "Over themselves" is a polite way of saying "over the Jews." The גמרא avoids saying it directly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עַל יְדֵי מָמוֹן — אֲסוּרָה לְבַעְלָהּ.
phrases.english: even because of money — she is forbidden to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the leniency in the משנה of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The money-case leniency applies only when Jews are in power. Under gentile control, even a woman jailed over money is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב from the woman held as collateral in אשקלון
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a teaching about a woman held as collateral for a debt in אשקלון. Witnesses said she was never secluded or defiled, and the Sages told her family to trust them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: רבי יוסי הכהן and רבי זכריה בן הקצב testified about a Jewish woman who was held as collateral in אשקלון. Her family kept away from her, but her witnesses testified that she was not secluded and not defiled. The Sages told the family: If you believe the witnesses that she was held as collateral, believe them that she was not secluded or defiled. And if you do not believe them that she was not secluded or defiled, do not believe them that she was held as collateral at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to test רב's rule. He quotes the whole case here, and the exact point of the challenge comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being held as collateral for a debt is a money case, the same type as in the משנה. רבא raises it against רב's strict limit. The Sages' reasoning is all-or-nothing: the same witnesses who told us she was taken as collateral are the ones saying she stayed pure, so you must accept both parts or neither.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (from a source)
She was taken as collateral (held as security for a debt)
They kept away from her
She was secluded (alone with a man)
She was defiled

steps.confusionAlert: The Sages are not saying to believe anyone about anything. They are saying the family cannot split the witnesses' words: the only source for "she was taken" is the same witnesses who say "she stayed pure."

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
Rabbi Yosei the Kohen testified
and Rabbi Zecharyah ben HaKatzav
about a Jewish woman who was held as collateral in Ashkelon,
and her family members kept away from her,
but her witnesses testified about her
that she was not secluded and was not defiled.
And the Sages said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the family members who kept away from her.

phrases.english: If you believe that she was held as collateral —
believe that she was not secluded and not defiled,
and if you do not believe
that she was not secluded and not defiled —
do not believe that she was held as collateral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רב's limit from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that under gentile control, even a woman jailed over money is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being held as collateral in אשקלון is a money case. רבא brings the Sages' ruling on it to test whether רב's strict limit fits. The exact clash is spelled out in the lines that follow.

steps.title: Ashkelon was under gentile control, yet the ruling was lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבא stresses that אשקלון was ruled by gentiles. That is exactly the situation where רב said even a money-case woman is forbidden. Yet the teaching gave a lenient ruling there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אשקלון is a place where the hand of the nations is strong over "themselves" (meaning over the Jews), and still it teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is pointing out the problem with רב's rule: the woman in the teaching was held in אשקלון, a city controlled by gentiles. This line sets up the contradiction, and the ruling it refers to comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that when gentiles are in power, even a woman held over money is forbidden to her husband (Step 8). אשקלון was a gentile-controlled city, so by רב's rule she should be forbidden. But the teaching from Step 9 treated her leniently and trusted the witnesses, so רבא sees a clash with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: "But look" or "but here". This opens a challenge by pointing to a known fact.
Literally "over themselves", a polite way of saying "over the Jews."
"And it teaches". This introduces the words of a משנה or ברייתא.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is giving a new case. He is still talking about the same אשקלון woman from Step 9. He is only adding one fact about the place: it was under gentile control. That fact is what makes it a challenge to רב.

phrases.english: But this was Ashkelon,
where the hand of the nations of the world
is dominant over themselves,
and yet it teaches:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's challenge from Step 9. It identifies the setting of that ברייתא as a gentile-controlled place.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule in Step 8: when gentiles are in control, even a woman held over money is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אשקלון was under gentile control, and the case was about money (a debt). By רב's rule the woman should be forbidden, but the teaching was lenient and trusted the witnesses.
